## Signatera™ Genome with Phased and Structural Variants Highlighted in ESMO Presidential Symposium, Supporting the Critical Role of MRD-Guided Treatment in Bladder Cancer


10/27/2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 127 KB](https://s201.q4cdn.com/354493536/files/doc_news/Signatera-Genome-with-Phased-and-Structural-Variants-Highlighted-in-ESMO-Presidential-Symposium-Supporting-the-Critical-Role-of-MRD-G-QI9VN.pdf)


*Natera’s oncology portfolio featured in 25 ESMO abstracts including 9 oral presentations, with publications in Nature Medicine and ESMO Open*


AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Natera, Inc.](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.natera.com&esheet=54629481&newsitemid=20261027424980&lan=en-US&anchor=Natera%2C+Inc.&index=1&md5=a4e7e59f840edaa22573dc4b04839bbd) (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today provided a summary of key findings from the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026. Following the presentation of several late-breaking datasets over the weekend, Natera’s technology was included in 25 abstracts, including 9 oral presentations, along with two concurrent publications.


Results from the **phase III** **VOLGA trial in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC)** were presented in a Presidential Symposium and highlighted Natera’s new Signatera Genome Assay with Phased and Structural variants. **** VOLGA evaluated a novel perioperative immunotherapy regimen and included an analysis of ctDNA dynamics before radical cystectomy. The results showed that Signatera ctDNA dynamics were highly predictive of event-free survival (EFS). Patients who were persistently Signatera-negative had a 24-month EFS rate of 91%, compared with 81% for those who started Signatera positive but cleared their ctDNA before surgery, and 55% for those who started positive and remained positive.


“Prior to radical cystectomy, patients who cleared their ctDNA as well as those who were persistently negative had excellent outcomes,” said Thomas Powles, MD, principal investigator of VOLGA and chair of Barts Cancer Centre at St. Bartholomew’s Hospital. “This supports our conviction that ultrasensitive ctDNA detection with Signatera can help guide treatment decisions in bladder cancer.”


Signatera has now been evaluated in seven phase III bladder cancer trials, spanning adjuvant immunotherapy, chemo-immunotherapy, and EV-based perioperative regimens. Across these trials, patients who stayed MRD-negative have consistently had excellent outcomes.


**Additional ESMO highlights**


- **Lung (MDT-Bridge,**[published in Nature Medicine](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nature.com%2Farticles%2Fs41591-026-04742-7&esheet=54629481&newsitemid=20261027424980&lan=en-US&anchor=published+in+Nature+Medicine&index=2&md5=87d3dffd8b2924dc1cab7127e7183899) **):** In resectable stage 2B–3B NSCLC, Natera’s Clarity TM MRD assay with phased variant technology detected ctDNA in 99% of patients before treatment. Clearance at cycle two of neoadjuvant therapy had an 83% predictive value for pathologic complete response. Clearance before surgery or chemoradiotherapy was associated with 100% 1-year EFS.
- **Endometrial (KEYNOTE-B21):** About 20% of patients with resected high-risk disease were Signatera-positive after surgery. Post-operative Signatera status had a 97% negative predictive value for disease-specific events in the pembrolizumab arm.
- **Breast (HER2-CR,**[published in ESMO Open](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.esmoopen.com%2Farticle%2FS2059-7029%252826%252902585-8%2Ffulltext&esheet=54629481&newsitemid=20261027424980&lan=en-US&anchor=published+in+ESMO+Open&index=3&md5=16a2db30ac3650fbcda8a6b297a9100b) **):** Among exceptional responders with HER2+ metastatic breast cancer, 81% maintained MRD-negativity during serial monitoring, supporting further study of Signatera-guided de-escalation.
- Additional studies were presented in colorectal cancer (SAGITTARIUS), gastroesophageal cancer (ICONIC), and more[as previously announced](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.natera.com%2Fcompany%2Fnews%2Fesmo-2026-presentations-deepen-the-evidence-base-for-nateras-oncology-portfolio-and-leadership-in-ultrasensitive-mrd-technology%2F&esheet=54629481&newsitemid=20261027424980&lan=en-US&anchor=as+previously+announced&index=4&md5=bbb93f331f2501cdaccebe7b9997b3a7) .


“This year’s ESMO program showcases the potential of ctDNA actionability at key decision points, including before cystectomy in bladder cancer and during neoadjuvant therapy in lung cancer,” said Minetta Liu, MD, Chief Medical Officer, Oncology and Early Cancer Detection, Natera. “Along with data in breast, gastroesophageal, colorectal and other cancers, this evidence highlights how ctDNA testing can guide patient care and improve cancer-related outcomes.”


**About Natera**


Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. We aim to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard-of-care to protect health and inform earlier, more targeted interventions that help lead to longer, healthier lives. Natera’s tests are supported by more than 400 peer-reviewed publications that demonstrate excellent performance. Natera operates ISO 13485-certified and CAP-accredited laboratories certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) in Austin, Texas, and San Carlos, California, and through Foresight Diagnostics, its subsidiary, operates an ISO 27001-certified and CAP-accredited laboratory certified under CLIA in Boulder, Colorado. For more information, visit[www.natera.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.natera.com&esheet=54629481&newsitemid=20261027424980&lan=en-US&anchor=www.natera.com&index=5&md5=e08c6362bc325c098f3e77c27e8308f1) .
